prize_parts.citation: for methods to estimate demand for differentiated products with endogenous prices and realistic substitution patterns, which made it possible to measure markups, mergers and policy effects empirically

statement.case_for: I keep B047 with Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes. Berry (1994) and Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (1995) solved a specific identification problem: price endogeneity combined with realistic substitution patterns across products. That made demand, markups and counterfactual policy effects recoverable from market-level data. It adds new empirical capacity and an explanatory framework that disciplines the data. In my view that combination is what makes a contribution prize-worthy. The work is about thirty years old. It is used beyond industrial organisation, in merger review, regulation, auctions, trade, health and environmental economics, so I do not read it as a narrow subfield tool. The credit trail points to three people, which is cleaner than most of the shortlist. My configuration is unchanged in ballot and names. I have kept the citation narrow and tied to demand estimation. I now list B006 ahead of B036 as my first alternative. Hassler's three-name file and the Kiyotaki-Moore core made me take B006 more seriously. The attribution problem I raised for B036 did not change. I would not make a two-name Kiyotaki-Moore prize my first preference. The criterion that keeps B047 ahead for me is the empirical record: BLP's identifying assumptions are explicit and have been probed repeatedly against outcomes such as merger retrospectives, whereas direct identification of the specific collateral channel is more mixed. I treat adjacency to the 2022 prize as a weaker consideration than that, because a distinct mechanism should not be penalised for sitting near a recently recognised field. I would apply the same standard to B023's overlaps with the 2021, 2023 and 2024 prizes. Everything here rests on background knowledge and not on verified citation data.
statement.case_against: The credit is cut. Bresnahan and Reiss (empirical entry and market structure) and Benkard and Levin (dynamic estimation) are credited on the ballot but cannot be included under the three-name limit. Pakes' share is probably larger than the other two names', so the trio is less symmetric than it looks. A citation centred on demand estimation gives little explicit weight to the dynamic-industry work. Counterfactuals such as markups and merger effects depend on functional-form and equilibrium assumptions, and a committee could reasonably see this as a method more than a substantive discovery. Finally, B006 with Kiyotaki and Moore alone has an equally clean originating core and arguably wider reach across macro, finance and policy modelling. I cannot show from the supplied evidence that B047 is the larger achievement. My preference rests on attribution clarity, maturity and the empirical record, and reasonable members weigh breadth of use differently.

responses.point: Hassler's own round-1 file prefers B006 with Kiyotaki, Moore and Gertler. He moved from a two-name opening to three because Gertler's intermediary-frictions work with Kiyotaki is separate from the Bernanke-Gertler accelerator. He wants the citation to name collateral constraints and balance-sheet frictions and to exclude bank-run and deposit-insurance themes. He also concedes that identification of the collateral channel is mixed and that Gilchrist is omitted.
responses.response: My round-1 reply described Hassler as proposing only Kiyotaki and Moore, which is not what his file says, so I am responding to the three-name version. His citation discipline answers much of my concern about the 2022 overlap. A citation anchored in collateral amplification and balance-sheet frictions is a distinct discovery from the bank-run work, and I now give the adjacency less weight than in my opening ranking. The part I still cannot resolve is Gertler. If his separable credit is the later intermediary work, the committee needs to name the specific papers that carry it, as the chair's questions ask. Without that, the two-name version is the defensible B006, and I would regard it as a serious alternative, not as my first choice. He also concedes that the specific collateral channel is empirically mixed. That is the criterion that keeps B047 ahead for me.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B006 first and B047 second. He argues that BLP's impact is concentrated in IO, antitrust and adjacent applied fields, while collateral and financial-friction mechanisms are part of the shared core of macro, finance and policy modelling. He says the omission of Bresnahan and Reiss is an attribution cost that B006 does not carry to the same degree.
responses.response: I accept the omission point. Under a three-name cap it is a real cost of B047, and I would want the citation to say openly that it recognises estimation methods and not the whole empirical-IO tradition. I would qualify the breadth argument. BLP-type demand estimation is routinely applied in trade, health, environmental and regulatory work, so its reach is not confined to IO. Breadth of use and breadth of conceptual influence are also different things, and you are right that B006 may score higher on the second. The chair asked what evidence would settle the weight. For me it is the record of validation against outcomes, and on that BLP has the longer applied track record. I regard this as a difference in weighting and not as a decisive scientific difference, and I do not count how many members rank either ballot first.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B047 first. He asks whether the committee will see it as industrial organisation or as econometric methodology. He would want the committee to confirm that the citation is for estimation methods and not for the whole field. He accepts that leaving out Bresnahan is a visible cost.
responses.response: I agree with the citation scope. I would classify B047 as an empirical method that is also a framework, because it ties estimation to an explicit model of differentiated-product competition. That is why I wrote the citation around demand estimation with endogenous prices and not around 'structural IO' in general. Whether the committee calls it IO or econometrics should not matter for merit, provided we apply the same standard we would to any methods candidate: does it solve a concrete problem, is the credit traceable to specific papers, and has it been checked in use? I think it meets that standard. I also accept your point that Bresnahan's omission is visible, and I would not hide it. The cap forces that cost, and it should be stated and not resolved by widening the group.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B047 first. He notes that Pakes' share is arguably larger than the other two names' shares and that the committee should say openly the citation recognises demand-estimation and dynamic-industry methods and not the whole empirical-IO tradition. He ranks B023 third and proposes only Autor and Hanson.
responses.response: I agree on the asymmetry. Pakes sits at the junction of the demand-estimation and dynamic-industry lines, so the trio is not equal shares, and a prize does not need to be. It does mean the citation should not imply that Berry and Levinsohn carry the dynamic-games work. I kept the wording on demand estimation for that reason. On B023 I do not share your two-name cut. My opening proposal was Autor, Hanson and Dorn. Dorn is a co-author of the central China-shock papers, and an Autor-Hanson pair would drop a co-originator to gain neatness. Even so, I agree with your reservation about bundling the technology and trade strands, and it is why B023 is not among my alternatives.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B006 first with Kiyotaki, Moore and Gertler and would accept a two-name award. She asks the IO specialists how large the omitted Bresnahan-Reiss contribution is, because that determines how clean the BLP trio really is. She also attributes to me a maturity concern about B031.
responses.response: I am not an IO specialist, so I will answer cautiously and from background knowledge. The Bresnahan-Reiss work on inferring competition from market structure is an earlier and distinct tradition, and it is substantial. I regard it as a separate achievement and not as a missing part of BLP, so its omission does not blur the BLP credit. It does mean the committee would be passing over a real contribution, and I would not call that cost small. If the committee wanted to honour that tradition, it would be a different configuration, and it could not be added to the BLP trio under the three-person cap. On B031, I rank it below my first choice on how settled the causal claims on place effects are, and I do not rely on that for my final preference.

uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers a prize recognising the Bresnahan-Reiss tradition or the Benkard-Levin dynamic-estimation line alongside or instead of BLP. The three-name cap leaves this unresolved.

Whether Gertler's post-accelerator intermediary work is separable from the Bernanke-Gertler line. This decides between a two-name and a three-name B006, and so how strong a competitor B006 is to B047.
How much weight breadth of conceptual influence (B006) should carry against a longer applied record of validation in use (B047). I do not claim a decisive scientific difference.

How sensitive BLP markup and merger counterfactuals are to functional-form and equilibrium assumptions, and how mixed the evidence on the specific collateral channel is. I rely on general knowledge, not independently verified citation, replication or usage data.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile for B047 or its credited names. My frequent co-authors (Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner, Bindler) are not credited names on any shortlisted ballot. My labour-economics field is near B023 and B031, neither of which is in my preferred configuration. For completeness, I presented the 2023 prize to Goldin at the announcement. Goldin is not a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, though Katz, credited on B023 and B031, is a known co-author of hers. I disclose this without adjudicating it, and it does not bear on B047 or on my alternatives B006 and B036.
